I’ve farmed my 6 mu of land in Quzhou for more than 50 years, and I stick to what I know. This year I’ll plant winter wheat and summer maize on all 6 mu — the wheat-maize double cropping system that every household around here relies on. I’m 71 now, only finished primary school, and I don’t bother much with those agricultural bulletins I can’t read well anyway. I learn by watching my neighbors: Old Wang uses Luyuan 502 wheat and Denghai 605 maize, and his yields are steady, so I’ll buy improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed too.

For the wheat, I’ll rotary till the soil in early October before sowing — that’s how we’ve always prepared the land here. I’ll apply about 19 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 11 kg of phosphorus and 3 kg of potassium, using urea and compound fertilizer like I did last year. I’ll irrigate four times: at sowing if the autumn is dry, then again at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I’ll spray pesticides four times in total — herbicide once and insecticide two or three times if the aphids show up. I expect around 1,000 kg per mu if the spring frost doesn’t hit too hard.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I have to get the maize in fast — there’s barely a week between crops. I’ll use no-tillage planting; the custom seeder can plant right into the wheat stubble. Maize needs less fertilizer here, so I’ll put down about 16 kg of nitrogen, 3 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. I’ll irrigate twice, once right after sowing and once at the big喇叭口 stage. For pesticides, three applications should do it — herbicide and insecticide. I’m hoping for about 950 kg per mu. I thought about planting cotton like some neighbors, but at my age the hand-picking is too hard on my back and my family can’t spare the labor, so wheat and maize it is.
